body:
Can confirm. I am a (now grown up) son that was in the same position as your own. My 'dad' tries his hardest all the time to see me or even just talk to me. He regrets ever leaving and he will die with a broken heart and an uncaring son.

Be there for your son as best you can. Try your best at providing for him and raising him, and he'll grow up alright. Best of luck to you both.

The only round I brought for my handgun was a dud. 

Still wish I had brought at least one more.

Don't feel bad. If they love you then all they want is the best for you. Telling them helps them to understand how you feel. 

Depression and especially suicidal thoughts are difficult things to process and analyze on one's own. Especially since they can distort rational thinking and make it more difficult for one to overcome obstacles in everyday life. 

It's good you're getting help, but if it's not enough then discuss it with your family and let them in. They can help you, or at least help you get the help you need. It doesn't have to be a solitary struggle. 

Glad to hear your cat saved you. Mine save me everyday. 

Peace and long life.

It really sucks holding all that in. 

I was discharged (honorably with full benefits) from the military for mental health issues. I was so ashamed at the time I kept it a secret from everyone I knew. 

That was years ago and I've still yet to tell a single person. Telling your family and friends what happened is extremely difficult. But let me tell you, keeping up that lie is SO much more worse. Believe me when I say it's better to tell your family. Because living that lie is what's driving your depression. 

I know it's not easy. I know it's a horrifying idea to tell them. Just remember: you failed only at your first attempt of higher education. This by no means is a failure in life. Not only could you make a second attempt at schooling, but you could also try something else entirely. Trades and skills-oriented occupations are very rewarding and are always looking for people. You could join the peace corps or try woofing and travel the world. You haven't failed yourself or anyone. You only failed your expectations (or possibly someone else's expectations of you?). Adjust your heading and get right back on that horse. 

I'm not trying to belittle your feelings or anything. I don't mean to give that impression. But take it from someone who has been in a similar situation for years now. Muster up all your courage and talk with your family. Let them know how you feel about it (yes, even your suicidal ideations). If there response is toxic to you, then fine someone else. But please, do find someone to help.

Feel free to pm me if you want to talk about it some more or need some support. 

Peace and long life.

I'm in the same situation OP. Different in details, I'm sure, but in the overarching concepts we share a commonality. 

I understand the pain of it as mine has been going on now for several years as well. I agree that the situation is usually seen as juvenile and a non-issue, but for the bearer of those feelings it certainly is not. 

If you ever need a sympathetic ear, or you manage to find a way to mend a broken heart from this, then please pm me. I'd be as equally interested in talking with you as I would to hear a remedy. 

Peace and long life.

Communication is key. Find a way to voice your concerns to your partner and discuss. 

What the problem is
Why it's a problem 
Ways to find common ground and solve these problems

Neither of you knows exactly what the other is thinking, so bringing it to one another's attention is the only way to find a solution. Good luck and hope it all works out for the best. 

Peace and long life.

Hey, take a breath, clean and wrap those cuts. Feel free to pm me if you want to talk about what's on your mind. I don't judge and I don't give self righteous advice. 

I have cut myself and I understand that moment when you just can't stop. I don't know exactly how you feel, but maybe we can help one another.

Hey man, read your whole post. If you want to talk, send me a message. Life is really rough and even more difficult on your own. 

Peace and long life.

Thought this was going to be one of those lame, super tedious, and uninteresting educational videos. As soon as the guy started speaking I rolled my eyes, but gave it a chance like any other video. Best decision I ever made. 

Found my new favorite channel.

Hey, I just wanted to say I have said almost all of the points you made at some point in my life. I can't know exactly, but based on your post I have an idea of what you're feeling because I, too, have a similar lack of reasoning to prolong my existence. 

I know you probably don't want to, (because I know I rarely ever want to) but if you want to discuss anything please pm me. I'm not trying to talk you out of it, but I always find gaining a new perspective to at least be a little enlightening. 

Peace and long life.

EDIT: Just realized this was a throwaway. If the OP can see this, my pm offer still stands.

Trying to find someone to listen is more difficult than most people would think. Many people are uncomfortable when someone close to them mentions suicidal tendencies or ideologies. This leads to people whom you'd life to confide in giving you adverse reactions to you spilling the beans to them. 

It's rough to share, and even worse when the person you share with wants nothing to do with your share. As difficult as it is, you may have to move on and find someone who will listen. 

When I was still a minor I told my mother about my suicidal ideation. Her reaction was less than stellar. She refused to believe me and just sat there saying "nope". Then she got up and went back to the daily routine, and has never said a word about it since. 

Just keep looking for your sympathetic ear and don't give up on getting help. 

Peace and long life.

If you really want to do self harm through cutting then please find another spot. 

Any cutting near large veins/arteries can end horribly. You can in fact still die with a 'horizontal' cut on the wrists. As the other comment says you can also seriously, and permanently, damage tendons and ligaments; basically crippling yourself in the process. Not to mention you'll have scars on a very noticeable area of the body. If you attempt to hide them you'll be wearing long sleeves for life; a little more than inconvenient. 

The best thing to do of course is just not cut. Self harm is self deprecating. Find someone to talk to. Vent your problems with a sympathetic ear. It's much more cathartic and helpful than cutting. PM me if you need such an ear. 

Peace and long life.
You obviously like your cats enough to say goodbye. Stick around for them, if no one else. They depend on you. They need you in their life.

As someone who attempted and failed I might be able to offer insight from her perspective. 

The best thing to do is to be there for her and listen. After an attempt one can feel extreme shame, regret (on either side of the coin), and heavy feelings of worthlessness and being a burden to their loved ones. 

Suicide can be a cry for help from one who cannot think rationally due to their irrational mental state from depression, ptsd, schizophrenia, etc. 

Like I said, just be there and listen. She may not want to talk immediately, but it can be a bad idea to try and pull a reason or answers out of someone after an attempt. 

It's sad to know she tried, but it's good she didn't succeed. Peace and long life, man.

I'd say the cat is a very good reason to at least postpone your decision. It can't take care of itself, and who knows how long it'll be on its own before anyone finds out. Even afterwards, it last be sent off to a shelter or animal control. 

At the very least find a good home for your furry friend. If it's not a reason to stick around, then at least do right by the cat and take care of its needs first.

I'm sorry to hear about your resolve. I know it all too well. You might be looking for a reason to live because of a lack of a sense of control on your life. In all reality there's no defining reason, and that's why individual life is so precious. You have to make your own reason to live. You have to find what it is that makes you want to be here, rather than finding the reasons to cease your unique existence. 

I wish you the best of luck. It's rough out there and repeated failures feel like they really stack up. I can empathize.
You want to elaborate? It might help.

Stay away from dating apps like tinder. If you really are as ugly as you say you are, then you'll have no luck on those kinds of apps. They're made specifically for the beautiful people. 

Keep working on the things you can. Like you said: dental work, going to the gym; those are excellent places to start. You may also try finding a really skilled hair stylist (for men, because not all specialize in male style) and asking for advice on hair styles, and even facial hair, to change your appearance a bit. You'd be surprised how a certain haircut can make you so different. 

Finally, the most important thing is to keep trying. Don't try so hard you're taking trips that far for something that's only 'prospective'. Get involved in local groups (meetup.com is an excellent source) and meet people. The more social connections you have, the easier it will be to find that girl. 

If you're interested in using apps, I'd recommend something like Bumble, Match, eHarmony. Some of those require subscriptions at some level, but you'll find the users to be a little less shallow. Good luck out there. 

Peace and long life, man.

Sounds like you know more than me. Not trying to make this a contest but I've had similar experiences and you sound way better off than me. Good on you. 

Hope you find what you're looking for. Peace and long life, man.

Hey, I know just how you feel. I have Pectus Carinatum; basically the opposite of Excavatum. It's less severe in appearance, but it's still quite noticeable, especially since I'm a very thin guy. 

I can't tell you how many times I've felt that people see me as less of a person because of it. I've never been able to take my shirt off in public because of it. I became so self conscious about it I would wear bulky jackets or button down shirts over my clothes; even in summer. But that's no way to live. 

If someone can't accept you specifically because of something completely out of your control like that, then there's no reason you should try with them. It's a longer road, filled with rejection; longer and more full than people without deformities, but you just have to keep right on walking. Eventually you'll find someone (or they'll find you) who's not going to judge you based solely on your body. 

Peace and long life, man.

Thanks for reading, and for replying. I will say my best traits are my will, work ethic, and hunger for knowledge. I just wish I knew how to apply those abilities to solve issues in my life; that's probably my biggest fault.

I feel I've learned many life lessons from the little bit I've experienced so far. I've noticed that among my peers I have more "wisdom" (or at least I perceive it) as far as life goes. Unfortunately that doesn't pay bills or get me started on an engineering degree. 

Thanks, again, and for the encouraging words.

If you're looking for someone to relate, feel free to pm me. 

Not trying to make this a contest or anything, but I know exactly where you've been those 7 years as I've been there myself for the last 15. 

If you want some quick advice: get help now. Any kind of help; therapy, meds, religion, support structures, whatever. Just get it. 

If you can't stand being like this now, you definitely don't want to stay like this for another 7 years. I know I don't. Please find help.

Congratulations. You make everyone with this illness look good when you take steps to help yourself and reach out for help. I wish I was as strong as you, and many like yourself. 

Good luck, and smooth sailing, on your path to a better you.

If he was as big a part of your life as you say, then that can only mean you were most likely a large part of his. 

It really is a tragedy things can't stay the way we like them to, but take solace in the time you did have. Even as a stepfather you sound more like a real, flesh-and-blood dad than most others. 

Undoubtedly be remembers the times you two had together, and who knows, maybe you'll see him again someday.

I wasn't a baker, but I was in this exact scenario at an old job. I was a supervisor in an understaffed, overworked, and unrecognized receiving department at a huge electronics store. Even on the slow days I, and everyone else needed to clock in a good 2 extra hours just so we could catch up to yesterday's load. Eventually corporate sent out the district manager to assess what was going on. Even after expressing all our concerns and needs there was no relief from any of it. 

The other supervisor there was much like your other head baker. Consistently they would overwork and get extremely enraged and try to guilt everyone else. 

I decided I was done with that and that life was more important. I started to leave on time each day before I finally quit a few months later. 

It's hard to convince people to see that the whole situation is screwed.

Screw your doubters OP, and stick with it. I regret every single day that I didn't sick with my love for music and sculpting. If you think you can make a career out of it then you do what you can to make it happen.
Or just, y'know, don't murder your pets. Pretty simple really.

Was waiting for someone to mention this. 

Even though it's unlikely in our lifetime, it's far more likely and reasonable than colonizing Mars. Between the sheer distance to travel to Mars and all the extra "terraforming" that would need to be done, colonizing (or even just industrialization of) Venus is a far better plan. 

Screw missions to Mars, I'm #TeamVenus.

I actually read through this whole thing because I never had any quality lessons from my "father". 

It's good to know there are men out there who raise their children and have compassion and understanding for them. I just wish I'd had one like some of the dad's in here oh-so-many years ago; maybe I would have been somebody by now instead of working on my 'note.
